Plasmodium parasites require pantothenate (Pan) from their hosts to synthesize coenzyme A (CoA), an essential metabolic cofactor. While blood-stage parasites can utilize both Pan and the immediate CoA precursor phosphopantetheine from mammals to synthesize CoA, mosquito-stage parasites rely critically on insect-derived Pan to synthesize CoA. Mosquito host pantothenate kinase (PanK), the rate-limiting enzyme in CoA biosynthesis, is therefore a promising drug target to reduce Pan bioavailability for parasite development. In support, we previously showed that the mammalian PanK activator PZ-2891 restricts Plasmodium yoelii and Plasmodium falciparum development in Anopheles stephensi. Two second-generation pantazines, PZ-3022 and PZ-3883, with improved stability significantly reduced Pan levels in A. stephensi at different time points post-treatment and had no effect on P. falciparum growth in vitro. In infection assays, mosquitoes provisioned with these pantazines exhibited markedly decreased midgut oocyst and salivary gland sporozoite burdens for both parasite species. These findings confirm that pantazines can effectively impair mosquito-stage parasite development and represent promising transmission-blocking small molecules.

43021434.resumo: In many insects, females exhibit behavioral changes after mating. This plasticity can be mediated by interactions between male-derived seminal fluid proteins (SFPs) and the female nervous system. The Drosophila melanogaster seminal fluid protein Sex Peptide (SP) causes mated females to sleep less during the day and consume more food than unmated females, among other behavioral changes. Although the SP-sensing neural circuits that convey information to the female's brain are known, the downstream neurons that affect post-mating behaviors remain unknown. P2 neurons in the fly's central brain are good candidates for regulating post-mating changes in sleep and food consumption, as they express feeding- and sleep-responsive neuropeptide F (NPF), directly innervate the fly's sleep center (the dorsal fan-shaped body, dFB), and are responsible for social-isolation-induced changes in sleep and food consumption. Using the GAL4/UAS system, we activated or silenced P2 neurons in mated and unmated females. We measured sleep duration using Drosophila Activity Monitors (DAM) and food consumption using Capillary Feeder (CAFE) and blue-dye assays. We found that P2-neurons are not responsible for post-mating changes in sleep and food consumption: mated females slept less during the day and ate more compared to unmated females irrespective of P2 neuron perturbation. Together, these results indicate that P2 neurons are unlikely to be primary downstream neurons through which male-transferred SP regulates post-mating sleep and food consumption. Future studies could determine whether P2 neurons regulate other post-mating behaviors or modulate sleep and feeding behaviors in a context-dependent manner.

43019102.resumo:
A 12-month longitudinal entomological study (September 2023-August 2024) in the Western Highlands of Cameroon (Penka-Michel) investigated malaria transmission dynamics and insecticide resistance markers, including target-site resistance (L1014F, N1575Y, G119S-Ace1) and metabolic resistance (E205D-CYP6P3, L119F-GSTe2, CYP6P9a/b) mutations. The study site was hyperendemic with an annual Entomological Inoculation Rate (EIR) of 839.5 infective-bites/human/year. Plasmodium falciparum predominated at 51.9% (68/131), though a significant non-falciparum burden was observed (P. malariae: 14.5%, 19/131; P. ovale: 15.3%, 20/131), including mixed infections (18.3%, 24/131). Anopheles funestus was the principal driver (Infection Rate, IR, of 7.8%) for P. falciparum and P. ovale curtisi, which peaked in the later rainy season (November). Anopheles gambiae (IR=5.4%) primarily vectored P. malariae, maintaining a sustained peak during the dry season (January). Widespread insecticide resistance was marked by high frequencies of target-site and metabolic resistance markers. Possible associations were observed between L119F-GSTe2 mutations with P. ovale curtisi transmission (IRR=1.15, p=0.03), and L1014F-kdr mutation with P. malariae (IRR=2.2, p=0.04). These dynamics underscore the intricate nature of a multifaceted, species-diverse system, where seasonal vector efficiency and insecticide resistance perpetuate the hyperendemicity of the frequently disregarded non-falciparum malaria species.

43019123.resumo: Diffusion-driven morphological instability, described by Mullins-Sekerka theory, predicts amplification of interfacial perturbations and wavelength selection for idealized sharp interfaces. However, natural systems rarely satisfy these assumptions. Here, we investigate barite mineralization on the growing interface of CO[Formula: see text] gas bubbles using 3D focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) tomography, quantitative surface analysis and reactive transport modelling. Bubble morphologies exhibit diffusion-driven instability, with dominant modes consistent with Mullins-Sekerka predictions. However, the interface violates key assumptions of the classical framework; it is porous, transport active, and evolves in pore space confinement, while crystallization proceeds via heterogenous nucleation, producing a polycrystalline interface. We show that diffusion-driven instability persists under these conditions but with modified mode selection, defining a non-classical Mullins-Sekerka regime for gas-liquid interface mineralization. Such dynamics influence pore structure evolution and transport pathways in the subsurface environment.

43015419.titulo: Strain-Specific Reduction of Ndel1 Enzymatic Activity During Early Zika Virus Infection in the Neonatal Brain
43015419.autores: de Farias IS, Ximenes AP, … Hayashi MAF (9 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during early development is associated with severe neurodevelopmental impairment, including congenital microcephaly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking viral exposure to neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Ndel1 (nudE neurodevelopment protein 1 like 1) is an oligopeptidase critically involved in neuronal migration, neurite outgrowth, and cytoskeletal dynamics, processes essential for proper brain development.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Using a neonatal intracerebroventricular infection model in Swiss mice at postnatal day 0, we compared the effects of a Brazilian ZIKV strain (ZIKVBR), an African lineage strain (ZIKVAF), and dengue virus (DENV) on Ndel1 regulation in the brain.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Building on previous observations that Ndel1 enzymatic activity is reduced in ZIKV-infected embryonic and neonatal brains, we investigated whether this modulation represents a conserved host response or a strain-specific molecular effect. We found that Ndel1 enzymatic activity was significantly reduced at early post-infection time points (P3 and P7) exclusively in ZIKVBR-infected animals, whereas ZIKVAF and DENV did not alter enzyme activity relative to controls. Notably, at the earliest timepoint (P3), this reduction occurred in the absence of changes in Ndel1 mRNA expression, indicating an initial post-transcriptional or functional mechanism of regulation, although Ndel1 mRNA expression was also significantly reduced by P7.

Ndel1 (nudE neurodevelopment protein 1 like 1) is an oligopeptidase critically involved in neuronal migration, neurite outgrowth, and cytoskeletal dynamics, processes essential for proper brain development. Building on previous observations that Ndel1 enzymatic activity is reduced in ZIKV-infected embryonic and neonatal brains, we investigated whether this modulation represents a conserved host response or a strain-specific molecular effect. Using a neonatal intracerebroventricular infection model in Swiss mice at postnatal day 0, we compared the effects of a Brazilian ZIKV strain (ZIKVBR), an African lineage strain (ZIKVAF), and dengue virus (DENV) on Ndel1 regulation in the brain. Importantly, this strain-specific reduction parallels the unique capacity of ZIKVBR to induce microcephaly and supports Ndel1 dysfunction as an early molecular event associated with neurodevelopmental impairment. Together, these findings identify a virus- and strain-specific regulation of a key neuronal enzyme and provide mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of ZIKVBR-associated neurodevelopmental outcomes.

43021391.resumo:
Understanding population connectivity in malaria vectors is important for surveillance in elimination settings, where local dispersal and population subdivision may influence residual transmission and the spread of adaptive traits. Anopheles albimanus is the major malaria vector in Honduras, yet its population structure remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to assess the genetic diversity and population structure of Honduran An. albimanus populations using microsatellite markers.
Adult mosquitoes collected from ten populations across Honduras (n = 176) were genotyped at eight species-specific microsatellite loci. Genetic diversity was estimated using the number of alleles, effective number of alleles, observed and expected heterozygosity, and Wright's fixation index. Population differentiation was evaluated using pairwise FST estimates and analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA). A hierarchical AMOVA was used to assess regional structure, and Bayesian clustering implemented in STRUCTURE was used to infer genetic clusters, with the most likely number of clusters determined using the Evanno ΔK method. Isolation by distance was tested with a Mantel test.
All loci were polymorphic and showed moderate to high genetic diversity (He = 0.513-0.817). Observed heterozygosity was consistently lower than expected, with widespread heterozygote deficits and frequent departures from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium across populations. Pairwise FST values ranged from 0.008 to 0.195, consistent with heterogeneous levels of genetic connectivity. AMOVA showed that 88% of genetic variation occurred within populations and 12% among populations (PhiPT = 0.117, P < 0.001), consistent with moderate but significant differentiation. Hierarchical AMOVA indicated minimal differentiation between La Mosquitia and the rest of Honduras (PhiRT = 0.012), while Bayesian clustering supported two inferred genetic clusters (K = 2) with evidence of admixture across populations, and Mantel analysis detected no evidence of isolation by distance.
Honduran An. albimanus populations harbor substantial genetic diversity while exhibiting moderate differentiation and fine-scale substructure despite overall connectivity. These findings are consistent with a model of partial connectivity shaped primarily by local population-level processes and illustrate the utility of microsatellite markers for detecting contemporary population structure relevant to malaria vector surveillance and control in elimination settings. Given the limited number of loci and the modest, cross-sectional sample, the structure reported here should be regarded as a conservative estimate of underlying population subdivision.

43014059.resumo: Although the live-attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine (TAK-003) is now available in Thailand, evidence on the behavioral determinants of its acceptance remains limited. We assessed TAK-003 vaccine acceptance, identified factors associated with acceptance using the Health Belief Model and Theory of Planned Behavior frameworks, and evaluated willingness to pay. We conducted a cross-sectional survey from December 2025 to February 2026. Thai adults aged 18-60 years who had never received a dengue vaccine were included and recruited through convenience sampling at Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok. Factors associated with vaccine acceptance were identified using multivariable binary logistic regression. A total of 448 participants were included, of whom 46.7% (n = 209) accepted the TAK-003 vaccine. In the adjusted model, participants aged 50-60 years (adjusted Odd ratio (aOR) = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.33-5.11), those with a history of dengue infection (aOR = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.56-4.35), greater perceived susceptibility (aOR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.02-2.41), greater perceived benefits (aOR = 2.57, 95% CI: 1.44-4.60), stronger cues to action (aOR = 2.33, 95% CI: 1.20-4.55), and more positive attitudes toward the vaccine (aOR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.06-2.84) were significantly associated with vaccine acceptance. Approximately 42.9% (n = 192) of participants were willing to pay ≤500 THB per vaccine dose. These findings may inform local strategies for communicating dengue risk and vaccine benefits and addressing affordability of TAK-003 vaccination.

43019095.resumo:
Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral illness that is responsible for increased rates of infection and major public health consequences, but no approved vaccine is available yet. This research employed an integrated approach of immunoinformatics and structural vaccinology to develop a promising multi-epitope subunit vaccine candidate. This study focused on the conserved structural polyprotein (NP_690589) for the purpose of epitope predictions. After strict filtering for high antigenicity, safety, and excellent conservation (> 90%), 9 CTL epitopes, 8 HTL epitopes, and 5 B-cell epitopes were selected. Chikungunya is an emerging arbovirus disease transmitted by mosquitoes of the genus Aedes, mainly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The tests were performed using a triplex kit (ZDC), a reagent that allows the simultaneous detection of the RNA of three arboviruses (chikungunya, dengue, and Zika).
Of the 5,821 samples tested, 107 cases were confirmed, representing a percentage of positivity case of 1.84%. Women accounted for 54.20% of confirmed cases. The most affected age group was 25-64 years old, with a frequency of 50.47%. No significant association was found between gender (p = 0.28), age (p = 0.73), and infection. The peak was observed in October, accounting for 34.58% of confirmed cases. The Kadiogo region was the most affected by the infection.
This study confirms the circulation of the chikungunya virus in Burkina Faso and highlights the importance of strengthening surveillance, improving diagnosis, and intensifying vector control to prevent outbreaks and better understand the dynamics of the virus.

Dengue is a climate-sensitive vector-borne disease that imposes a substantial public health burden in tropical and subtropical regions. Temperature, rainfall, and extreme weather can affect mosquito ecology, human exposure, and the environmental suitability for transmission. This study characterized the global research landscape of dengue and extreme weather and examined whether country-level research output corresponded to dengue burden and climate-driven vector suitability.
The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on 22 May 2026. Publication trends, collaboration networks, journals, authors, co-cited references, citation bursts, keyword patterns, and thematic evolution were examined using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package. Country-level publication output was linked to estimates from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 dataset, the socio-demographic index for 2021, and mean index-p values for 1990-2022. Associations between publication output and dengue burden were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation among countries classified as dengue-endemic.
A total of 290 publications from 2008 to 2026 met the eligibility criteria. Annual publication output increased overall and remained comparatively high after 2020. The United States contributed the largest number of publications, followed by China, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Brazil. The literature connected tropical medicine and infectious disease epidemiology with environmental health, climate science, vector ecology, modeling, and public health. Major themes included climate change, temperature, rainfall, the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, extreme weather, Aedes vectors, transmission modeling, risk prediction, and early warning. Among 80 countries classified as dengue-endemic, publication output was positively correlated with the age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) in 2023 (Spearman's ρ = 0.32, P = 0.004, n = 80) and the disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) rate in 2023 (ρ = 0.36, P < 0.001, n = 80). In contrast, its association with the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) in ASIR from 1990 to 2023 was not statistically significant (ρ = 0.20, P = 0.070, n = 80). Several dengue-endemic countries with comparatively high disease burden or long-term climate-driven vector suitability had no eligible Web of Science-indexed publications in the present dataset.
Research on dengue and extreme weather has expanded, and publication output showed modest positive associations with contemporary dengue burden among dengue-endemic countries. However, research output was not significantly associated with the long-term trend in dengue incidence, and substantial geographic disparities remained. The separate assessment of burden, research output, and climate-driven vector suitability identified geographic areas that may warrant closer consideration when research capacity, surveillance support, and equitable international partnerships are developed.

These findings were consistent with severe dengue, active Graves' disease, and Hashimoto's thyroiditis. The patient received comprehensive supportive care, including continuous hemodynamic monitoring, gastric mucosal protection, antipyretic therapy, cautious fluid resuscitation, and careful management of the electrolyte and acid-base balance. Methimazole was administered to control thyrotoxicosis. Her clinical condition gradually improved, and she was discharged in stable condition with endocrinology follow-up arranged.

Descriptive patterns suggested variation in timeliness across countries; however, the small number of country-level observations precluded confirmatory statistical inference.

Findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating because of purposive sampling, retrospective data reconstruction, ecological country-level analysis and the small number of observations. 43022950.resumo: Dengue is a major public health concern in tropical and sub-tropical areas of the world. Dengue virus is transmitted to humans primarily by female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and its epidemiology is heavily influenced by the climate. We developed a mechanistic compartmental model to characterize how climate and the evolution of population-level immunity influence changes in the epidemiology of dengue. The model explicitly incorporates aquatic and adult stages of the mosquito vector and cross-immunity (to another serotype) to better represent the transmission of dengue compared to previous models. It incorporates parameters related to mosquito development, behaviour, and mortality that are dependent on temperature, rainfall, and humidity. We calibrated the model to available dengue seroprevalence estimates for Dhaka, Bangladesh as it is a well-observed densely populated endemic area for dengue and will be strongly impacted by climate change. We then simulated dengue epidemiology for the period of 1995-2014 and compared the simulation output with available epidemiologic data. The model produced repeating annual outbreaks of dengue with strong seasonality, as observed in the dengue case reports for Dhaka. The median number of annual dengue infections produced by the model was 1.6 million (IQR: 0.6-2.3 million) and the median of the annual daily peak size of dengue infections was 24,121 (IQR: 7,807-39,308) across the simulations. These figures while exceeding reported cases in Dhaka, which do not include asymptomatic infections or cases not seeking healthcare, align with previous estimates. The modelled seroprevalence of 62% (IQR: 58-75%) aligned with survey results from Dhaka. In most model simulations, dengue infections occurred during August to December with the median peak occurring in October. The model outputs demonstrated a high degree of conformity to the reported data in terms of seasonality, and seroprevalence, indicating that the model provides a good representation of overall dengue epidemiology in Dhaka. By accounting for climate variables, host immunity, and their interplay, our model is well-suited for evaluating the long-term impact of climate change on dengue transmission in Dhaka and other settings where climate and epidemiological data are available.

43021958.resumo:
The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, is responsible for acute febrile illness and severe polyarthralgia. Although both innate and adaptive immune responses influence the disease outcomes, the detailed cellular immunopathogenesis of CHIKV in peripheral blood is not yet fully elucidated.
We profiled PBMCs from 29 patients with acute CHIKV infection and 10 controls via single-cell RNA sequencing. Between-group analyses treated donors as biological replicates, incorporating pseudobulk differential expression analysis as well as donor-level comparisons of pathway scores and cell proportions. Orthogonal validation was performed using qPCR and ELISA, and an exploratory analysis was conducted on a publicly available DENV dataset.
Interferon-response signatures were upregulated across the majority of PBMC populations, with particularly prominent signals observed in monocytes and NK cells. Differences in relative cell composition were detected in descriptive statistics, but did not retain statistical significance after donor-level multiple testing correction. B-cell immunoglobulin isotypes varied across cell subsets, and their transcripts did not allow determination of antigen specificity. Cross-study analysis of DENV did not support the quantitative conclusion that the CHIKV-induced immune response is stronger.
Acute CHIKV infection is associated with a broad interferon-stimulated transcriptional program in PBMCs. Conclusions drawn from cross-sectional and cross-study comparisons require cautious interpretation.

43023846.resumo: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can persist in the host for prolonged periods. Biofilm formation represents a key strategy that promotes bacterial persistence, enhances antibiotic resistance, and facilitates immune evasion. Thus, targeting biofilm formation holds significant therapeutic potential for tuberculosis. Exopolyphosphatase 1 (PPX1), highly conserved among mycobacteria, hydrolyzes inorganic polyphosphate. Although changes in polyphosphate levels are known to influence mycobacterial biofilm formation, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In this study, using a Mycobacterium smegmatis model strain, we found that the level of polyphosphate in the Δppx1 mutant significantly increases, concomitant with impaired biofilm formation. Further investigation revealed that elevated polyphosphate enhances the transcriptional activity of the transcription factor RegX3, which in turn represses biofilm formation. Mechanistically, activated RegX3 directly binds to and upregulates the dcpA gene, encoding a bifunctional enzyme that lowers intracellular cyclic di-GMP levels. This reduction ultimately perturbs cell wall lipid synthesis and compromises biofilm formation. In summary, this work reveals a signaling pathway through which polyphosphate governs biofilm formation in M. smegmatis.

43021904.resumo:
Insect hemocytes play a crucial role in the innate immune response against pathogens. However, transcriptomic profiling and analysis of hemocytes in insect vectors, such as Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes, are challenging due to their small size, low RNA content, limited numbers, and highly reactive nature.
To address these challenges, we developed a protocol for single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing of stabilized hemocytes from adult female An. gambiae mosquitoes. Immediate stabilization of hemocytes following perfusion prevents transcriptional changes during sample collection and RNA degradation, thereby minimizing technical artifacts. After stabilization, hemocytes are filtered to remove contaminating tissue and ambient RNA introduced by tissue injury during sample collection, enriching for hemocyte-specific transcripts. The stabilized hemocytes can be stored for up to four weeks, allowing for convenient sample storage, transportation, and simultaneous processing of multiple samples, which reduces costs and minimizes batch effects.
Our single-cell RNA sequencing stabilization and processing protocol is compatible with the 10X Genomics platform, yielding high-quality and reproducible data. We demonstrate higher hemocyte recovery compared to other contemporary methods, enabling the identification of rare hemocyte populations. However, this protocol requires further optimization to increase the recovery of small-sized prohemocytes (< 5 μm in diameter). Our bulk mRNA stabilization and hemocyte enrichment protocol yields high-quality, intact RNA, and Illumina bulk mRNA sequencing libraries enable an in-depth investigation of gene expression changes in hemocytes. These protocols significantly improve transcriptomic analysis of hemocytes, which is critical for advancing discoveries in vector biology and disease control. Moreover, the protocol can be applied to other mosquito species and likely many other insects with only minor optimizations.

43014143.resumo: Accurate and sensitive point-of-care diagnosis of malaria, with the ability to distinguish co-infections among Plasmodium species responsible for the disease, is critical for malaria control programs. Species-specific identification is essential for selecting appropriate therapies and preventing recurrence. Moreover, easier and non-invasive infection detection can dramatically reduce the number of infected cases and minimize the pandemic's public health and economic impact. Here, we present a graphene electrolyte-gated field-effect transistor array for a DNA biosensor that enables highly sensitive detection of DNA from five Plasmodium species. The 21-channel chip, grouped into 7 regions for multiplex detection, integrates non-covalently functionalized graphene with ssDNA probes targeting each species. The miniaturized readout platform allows direct and amplification-free measurements upon deposition of small volumes of analyte. Synthetic target DNA was detected in both physiological buffer and 25× diluted saliva with attomolar limit of detection, dynamic ranges spanning more than four orders of magnitude, and sensitivities of ∼16-19 mV/decade. Notably, DNA extracted from P. falciparum cultured parasites, spiked into human saliva, was reliably detected down to ∼10 aM. A mixed-target multiplex experiment on a single chip with 7 functionalized areas demonstrated the absence of target cross-talk. Accelerated ageing experiment at 75% relative humidity or 65 °C showed chips keep their analytical performance. This platform enables direct, amplification-free identification of multiple malaria species, in non-invasive samples. Its combination of sensitivity, specificity, and portability positions this biosensor as a powerful tool for early malaria screening and species differentiation in resource-limited or field settings.

43014523.resumo: Cholesterol is distributed unevenly across the membranes of erythrocytes infected with Plasmodium falciparum. Earlier imaging and biochemical studies described a relative inward sterol gradient and implicated dilution by parasite-produced lipids. Genetics, localisation, structural studies and cholesterol-analogue efflux assays have since identified PfNCR1 as a determinant of parasite plasma membrane sterol homeostasis. This Review integrates these findings with evidence on host membrane properties, parasitophorous vacuolar membrane formation and membrane expansion during intracellular development. It distinguishes observed redistribution from inferred membrane topology, relative sterol enrichment from absolute cholesterol mass, and transport capacity from the direction and magnitude of flux in infected cells. Cholesterol-dependent invasion phenotypes may reflect membrane mechanics, receptor organisation or cytoskeletal coupling without requiring cholesterol translocation. Likewise, phospholipid expansion can reduce the cholesterol-to-phospholipid ratio without net sterol loss. The resulting partitioning model is an integrative conceptual synthesis, rather than a newly discovered gradient or an experimentally established complete cholesterol-trafficking pathway. Its unresolved steps define opportunities for compartment-resolved measurements and selective therapeutic investigation.

43019357.resumo: Although Plasmodium falciparum is the most prevalent and highly virulent species in Sub-Saharan Africa, non-falciparum species are increasingly recognized as a hidden burden. Generally, infections caused by non-falciparum species occur with low parasite densities and often present as co-infections with P. falciparum. These parasites may evade detection by routine diagnostics, complicating malaria case management and control efforts. To investigate the distribution of different Plasmodium parasites, we analysed 5,314 randomly selected samples from 18,969 samples collected across all 26 regions of Mainland Tanzania in 2023. Plasmodium parasites were detected using 18S qPCR. Of the analyzed samples, 52.3% (n = 2,780) were positive for any Plasmodium species. P. falciparum was detected in 51.2% (2,719/5,314), P. malariae in 1.4% (76/5,314), and P. ovale spp. in 1.8% (98/5,314) of the samples. Mixed infections were detected in 2.0% (107/5,314), with P. malariae and P. falciparum in 0.8% (40/5,314), and P. ovale mixed with P. falciparum in 1.1% (61/5,314) of the samples analysed. Among the samples with positive results (n = 2,780), mono-infections were detected at 93.9% (2,612/2,780) for P. falciparum, 1.1% (30/2,780) for P. malariae, and 1.1% (31/2,780) for P. ovale spp., respectively. Unlike P. malariae and P. ovale, P. falciparum infections were significantly influenced by transmission intensities, with the highest odds in regions with high transmission intensities compared to those with low (OR=1.61, p < 0.001), and very low transmission (OR=1.48, p < 0.001). School children had higher odds of P. falciparum infections compared to adults (OR=1.56, p < 0.001) and under-fives (OR=1.47, p < 0.001). Adults were also less likely to have P. malariae infections than schoolchildren (OR= 0.45, p = 0.021).The findings of the first-ever nation-wide survey reveal a high prevalence of P. falciparum, low prevalence of non-falciparum species, and complex species landscape. They underpin the need to expand surveillance systems beyond P. falciparum and adapt interventions to target all Plasmodium species.

Importantly, it also detected 8 of 14 P. falciparum infections suspected to carry hrp2/3 deletions, which caused false-negative RDT results, comparable with microscopy. This is the first study to evaluate XN-31 for detecting asymptomatic infections, non-P. falciparum species, and hrp2/3-deleted parasites, which are key diagnostic challenges in endemic settings. Our findings support the potential of XN-31 as a practical and reliable surveillance tool that bridges between RDTs and PCR for enhanced parasite detection and accelerated malaria control efforts.

We used a randomized experiment to examine the effects of subsidies for a mosquito repellent ointment that protects against mosquito bites and malaria on product use and malaria cases in Burkina Faso. We find no substitution with bed nets, but a strong effect on the use of mosquito coils. The treatment effects on usage are heterogeneous, including more positive outcomes for young children as reported by their caregiver. The impact on use continues even after the end of the subsidy, with effects on demand and willingness to pay elicited through a Becker-DeGroot-Marschak approach eight months after the end of the intervention. Our intervention induces a significant reduction in declared malaria occurrence during the rainy season, but no effect at the very end of the rainy season when blood tests were taken. The seemingly discrepancy will be partly explained by timing and sample size.

43020197.resumo: Malaria transmission and burden exhibit substantial spatial and age-related heterogeneity that is often obscured by national-level modeling approaches. In this study, we develop a spatially explicit, age-structured malaria transmission and burden model designed to operate at the subnational scale (Admin-1) while remaining fully consistent with national-level estimates. The model integrates monthly age cohorts (0-100 years), naturally acquired immunity, heterogeneous entomological inoculation rates (EIR), and key non-vaccine interventions, allowing a fine-scale representation of malaria dynamics across space, time, and age. Subnational EIRs are inferred from malaria prevalence in children aged 2-10 years, while age-specific clinical progression and mortality are modeled through immunity-dependent transitions. To ensure national-subnational consistency despite nonlinear transmission dynamics, a parsimonious rescaling framework is introduced, based on time-varying country-level-to-subnational ratios of estimated cases and deaths, ensuring consistency between subnational projections and national burden trajectories. Model calibration is performed using a joint root-mean-square error (RMSE) metric that pools discrepancies across cases and deaths across all administrative units and years. Applying the model to both high- and low-transmission settings (Benin, Burkina-Faso, Ethiopia, and Somalia) successfully reproduces observed national and subnational dynamics, while revealing strong and persistent spatial heterogeneity within countries. The model captures marked geographical gradients in EIR and localized epidemic hotspots. The resulting framework provides a flexible platform for analyzing spatial heterogeneity in malaria transmission, age-specific burden, and intervention impact, and is well-suited for prospective analyses, including the evaluation of vaccination strategies, targeted intervention deployment, and long-term burden projections.

43021257.resumo: Rodent malaria parasites have long served as essential experimental models for understanding human malaria, yet little is known about their ecology and evolution in the wild. The thicket rat Grammomys poensis (formerly Thamnomys rutilans) is considered the main natural host of murine Plasmodium species in Central Africa. This study aimed to establish a long-term field site to investigate Plasmodium-Grammomys interactions under natural conditions in southeastern Gabon. Over a period of 3 years, trapping was conducted across twelve forest fragments in the Batéké Plateau region using both Tomahawk traps and direct collection at nest. Despite an intensive effort (18,000 trap-nights and 1380 nests inspected), only 20 adult Grammomys were captured, all by collection directly at nest. None were infected with Plasmodium as determined by two sensitive nested-PCR assays targeting the cytb gene, suggesting extremely low transmission or absence of parasite circulation in the study system. These results contrast with earlier studies reporting high infection prevalence in Grammomys from other Central African regions. The absence of infection may reflect local extinction of Plasmodium lineages, limited vector exposure due to the absence of species feeding on arboreal rodents, or host resistance. Because the rodent malaria lines currently used as experimental models in laboratories worldwide were isolated decades ago and have since been maintained through serial passage, access to recent field isolates would be highly valuable for capturing contemporary natural diversity and for enhancing the ecological, evolutionary, and biomedical relevance of these model systems. This study highlights both the challenges of studying this host-parasite system in the wild and the possibility that rodent Plasmodium transmission in this system may be more spatially and ecologically constrained than previously assumed.

43021517.resumo: Malaria is the leading cause of death and economic burden worldwide. Current diagnostic methods rely on microscopy and blood-based rapid diagnostic tests. A common rapid diagnostic test target is Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (PfHRP2), a parasite protein released into the host's blood during Plasmodium infection; it has also been detected in saliva, although results have been inconsistent. This pilot study quantified plasma and salivary PfHRP2 antigen levels and assessed their associations with age, parasite density, and clinical malaria status in a malaria-endemic region of western Kenya with high transmission. This pilot study enrolled 34 patients with acute uncomplicated malaria. Paired blood and saliva samples were collected at enrolment, with repeat sampling 4 weeks after treatment. P. falciparum infection was confirmed by light microscopy, and PfHRP2 concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Data were analyzed in R version 4.5.2. Spearman's rank correlation and robust linear regression were used to examine the relationship between plasma and salivary P. falciparum antigen levels in individuals with acute malaria and to assess whether PfHRP2 concentrations in either matrix predicted parasite density, clinical malaria status, and age. Salivary PfHRP2 levels did not significantly predict parasite density or age (χ²=0.54, P=0.76). By contrast, plasma PfHRP2 levels strongly predicted both parasite density and age (P=0.034). Plasma and salivary PfHRP2 concentrations were not significantly correlated (ρ=-0.327, P=0.059). Nevertheless, routine measurement of salivary PfHRP2 using more sensitive methods may improve diagnosis and guide treatment management.

43019368.resumo: Chandipura virus (CHPV), an emerging rhabdovirus endemic to India, causes acute encephalitis, primarily in children. In 2024, India experienced its worst CHPV outbreak in 20 years (245 cases, 33% fatal). Sandflies (family Psychodidae, subfamily Phlebotominae) are considered the primary vectors, but experimental evidence suggests mosquitoes can support infection under laboratory conditions. Animal host species involved in natural transmission remain unknown. We conducted this PRISMA-guided scoping review to identify evidence of natural CHPV infection in animals and arthropods to assess surveillance and emergence potential. Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and Google Scholar, and three Indian databases (Shodhganga, Krishikosh and CeRA), were searched using predefined terms. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed primary research detecting evidence of CHPV infection (antigen, RNA or antibodies) in arthropods and non-human vertebrate hosts, excluding experimental infection studies. Two reviewers independently screened records, then extracted data on species, location, detection methods and prevalence or seroprevalence. Of 451 screened records (747 total with 296 duplicates removed), 11 met the inclusion criteria. Direct evidence of CHPV infection was reported in phlebotomine sandflies in India, Senegal and Kenya, with low inferred infection prevalence even in outbreak-associated investigations. No evidence was found of natural CHPV infection in wild mosquito or tick populations. Indirect evidence of CHPV exposure (neutralising antibodies) was reported in several livestock species (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, pigs), dogs and wild toque macaques, and virus was isolated from a single African hedgehog. In conclusion, direct detection of CHPV in sandflies is consistent with their role as vectors, yet the broader animal host range, their role in virus maintenance and amplification, and the ecological drivers of transmission are incompletely understood. This review highlights the need for integrated One Health surveillance and targeted host-vector studies as globalisation and environmental change promote the spread and redistribution of competent vectors.

43015803.resumo: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier and refractory hypoxemia. Despite advances in supportive care, effective targeted therapies remain lacking. We also discuss candidate biomarkers, approaches for clinical stage and phenotype identification, therapeutic opportunities, and current evidence limitations, aiming to provide a conceptual framework for stage-specific and precision interventions in ARDS. We further contextualize existing and controversial immunomodulatory strategies, including corticosteroids and IL-6/IL-1 blockade, within this dynamic framework to illustrate how disease stage and patient phenotype may influence therapeutic responses. Throughout the review, we distinguish evidence derived from experimental models from observational data in human ARDS and separately identify human interventional evidence and therapies supported by current clinical guidelines.

Spodoptera frugiperda, commonly known as the fall armyworm (FAW), is a pest of great economic importance in corn. The species has recently expanded from the Western Hemisphere to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, increasing its global impact. FAW has diverged into two strains, corn and rice, which differ in genetics, reproductive isolation, resistance to insecticides and to Bacillus thuringiensis, and, more recently found, in their microbiota. Endosymbionts such as Arsenophonus and Spiroplasma have been detected using next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the 16S rRNA gene. However, information on additional endosymbionts and their transmission dynamics remains limited. Therefore, the objectives of this study were to (i) evaluate the presence of endosymbionts such as Arsenophonus, Cardinium, Spiroplasma, and Wolbachia as well as the intracellular parasite Microsporidia, throughout the life cycle of both strains of S. frugiperda, (ii) assess their potential vertical transmission, and (iii) examine possible associations between these symbionts and life-history traits in this insect.
Larvae were sampled from corn and rice fields in central and eastern Colombia. Laboratory colonies of the corn and rice strains of S. frugiperda were maintained under controlled conditions. Strain identity was confirmed using diagnostic molecular markers (MspI, SacI, FR). Within each strain, one-to-one crosses were performed to construct life cycle tables and estimate life-history traits components. DNA was subsequently extracted from parental individuals and from eggs, larvae, pupae, and adults. Following extraction, conventional and real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) using an intercalating dye were conducted to identify the genera Arsenophonus, Cardinium, Spiroplasma, and Wolbachia, the intracellular parasite Microsporidia and positive amplifications were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
Arsenophonus was detected exclusively in the corn strain using conventional PCR and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Additionally, Spiroplasma was detected in both strains using real-time PCR using an intercalating dye. The detection of these endosymbionts across developmental stages is consistent with, vertical transmission. Differences in life-history traits components were observed between the two strains, but no clear association was detected between these differences and the presence of either endosymbiont under the conditions evaluated. These results highlight the need for further studies to evaluate the potential role of endosymbionts in the biology of this pest and to further on to better understand their transmission dynamics and possible ecological interactions.

43012319.resumo: Bees and wasps are ecologically vital, but many species are declining owing to anthropogenic stressors. Social bees harbour host-specific and dense gut microbiomes that affect their resilience to stress. However, there are tens of thousands of other bee and wasp species that vary in sociality and diet (including pollen-feeding and predatory guilds), traits known to influence host-microbe symbioses. Here, we measured the composition and absolute abundance of bacterial communities in adult metasomas across 61 genera and 14 families of field-collected bees, predatory wasps and pollen wasps. We found that solitary bees and both wasp guilds harbour distinct bacterial taxa and lower bacterial abundances as compared with social bees. Bacterial abundances also varied extensively among and within genera of solitary bees, with little variation explained by body size, diet breadth or nesting ecology. Furthermore, microbiome composition was only weakly differentiated among solitary bees and the two wasp groups, even when comparing herbivorous (pollen-feeding) and omnivorous taxa. We suggest that the sparse and somewhat stochastic microbiomes of solitary bees and wasps reflect weak host dependence on microbially mediated functions, a trait that may influence their responses to environmental change.

43012953.resumo: Microbial communities are frequently exposed to environmental disturbances, yet recovery does not always lead to a single, predictable outcome. Distinguishing resilience, the capacity to recover following perturbation, from reliability, the predictability of that recovery, is essential for understanding microbiome dynamics. Here, we investigated cross-generational gut microbiome responses in the red flour beetle, Tribolium castaneum, a globally significant stored-product pest exposed to frequent environmental and dietary shifts. Using a four-generation experimental design (G0-G3), we examined how gut microbial communities respond to a major environmental transition from commercial to laboratory rearing, followed by dietary perturbations. The shift to laboratory conditions produced the largest change in gut microbiome composition, occurring within a single generation and exceeding the effects of dietary shifts. Following this disturbance, microbial communities stabilized across subsequent generations, consistent with strong ecological resilience. However, recovery trajectories and endpoints differed among treatments, with replicate lineages stabilizing toward multiple, partially distinct community configurations rather than a single shared state, indicating low reliability. Diet influenced overall community composition and diversity trajectories, but these effects were smaller in magnitude than the dominant generational restructuring. Together, these results show that the T. castaneum gut microbiome is resilient but not strictly reliable, stabilizing after rapid reorganization toward multiple partially distinct community configurations associated with environmental history rather than a single shared state. These findings underscore the importance of environmental context in shaping host-associated microbiomes and suggest that the capacity for rapid microbiome restructuring may contribute to the ecological success of insect pests in variable environments.

43015466.resumo: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1-5. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal-immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

43018858.resumo: Obesity is a chronic immunometabolic disorder associated with alterations in biological aging pathways and increased risks of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Obesity and chronological aging share several characteristics, including low-grade inflammation, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, epigenetic alterations, and immune remodeling. However, these similarities do not necessarily establish accelerated biological immune aging. This review critically evaluates obesity-associated immunosenescence, metaflammation, and multiorgan dysfunction by examining supporting and conflicting findings, alternative explanations, methodological limitations, and therapeutic evidence. Although experimental and observational studies report alterations in lymphocyte differentiation, innate immune function, inflammatory signaling, and selected biological-age markers, these findings are not uniformly observed across immune-cell populations, tissues, or metabolic phenotypes. Metabolically healthy obesity, tissue-dependent epigenetic aging, and differences between human and animal findings challenge the interpretation of obesity as a universal accelerator of immunosenescence. Furthermore, chronological age, cytomegalovirus infection, sex-related differences, adiposity distribution, and metabolic comorbidities complicate attributing immune alterations specifically to obesity. The proposed immunosenescence-metaflammation-multiorgan dysfunction framework therefore remains a testable mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established causal pathway. Although immune-cell phenotypes, epigenetic clocks, inflammatory mediators, and multi-omics signatures may help characterize obesity-associated immune dysfunction, their specificity, longitudinal validity, and clinical utility remain insufficiently established. Nutritional interventions, exercise, bariatric surgery, and pharmacological treatments can improve selected metabolic and inflammatory outcomes, but these improvements do not necessarily demonstrate sustained reversal of biological immune aging. By critically comparing supportive evidence with contradictory observations and unresolved causal relationships, this review identifies the principal limitations of current mechanistic, biomarker, and therapeutic research. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal immune profiling, direct functional assessment, tissue- and sex-specific analyses, causal validation, and controlled interventions incorporating validated immune-aging endpoints to determine whether premature immune aging is a measurable and therapeutically modifiable consequence of obesity.

Isthmin-1 (ISM-1), an immunometabolic adipokine, has not been adequately studied in chronic HBV infection. ROC analysis showed moderate overall performance (AUC = 0.656); the marker exhibited a remarkably high sensitivity (97.0%) but limited specificity (38.7%).
Serum ISM-1 levels are significantly reduced in chronic HBV infection and are inversely associated with viral replication. The positive correlation with direct bilirubin may reflect an adaptive cellular response to hepatocellular stress rather than simple dysfunction. Despite its limited specificity, the high sensitivity of ISM-1 suggests that it could be a valuable complementary tool for monitoring disease progression and viral status in clinical practice.

The yarns were braided and woven into scaffolds supporting cell adhesion and proliferation. This high-performance alternating-current electrospinning approach effectively bridges the gap between electrospun fibers-whose two of three characteristic dimensions reside in the nanoscale-and macroscopic textile manufacturing, thereby enabling a practical and scalable pathway for the industrial production of nanofiber yarns for biomedical and advanced material applications.

Clinical intervention evidence remains limited and does not establish structural disease modification. Translation requires verified metabolite exposure, cell-specific target engagement, functional validation of cell death, and longitudinal assessment of imaging, pain, and disability. This evidence-based distinction provides a framework for prioritizing testable gut-disc mechanisms and clinically relevant interventions.

ensaio.historia:
Durante quase um século, a parasitologia molecular operou sob um dogma redutor: para entender por que um mosquito transmite ou bloqueia a malária, ou por que o camundongo desenvolve edema cerebral, deveríamos buscar sempre "o gene" ou "a citocina". Mapeamos vias inteiras (Toll, Imd, JAK-STAT), sequenciamos transcriptomas de células únicas e quantificamos centenas de RNAs mensageiros.

No entanto, uma pergunta desconfortável permaneceu sem resposta na bancada: **como decisões vitais de infecção ocorrem em frações de segundo, muito antes de qualquer RNA polimerase conseguir transcrever um gene?**

Quando o oocineto atinge o microvilo do mosquito, a digestão do sangue está no auge. Milhões de eritrócitos se rompem, gerando uma pressão coloidosmótica massiva, liberação letal de hemo livre e fluxo turbulento não-newtoniano. O parasito não tem horas para esperar uma via gênica ser ativada. Ele precisa explorar as propriedades biofísicas nativas do epitélio: diferenças de potencial elétrico entre células vizinhas, zonas de menor tensão mecânica e condensação líquida de proteínas de superfície.

Se quisermos descobrir o que não sabemos que existe, precisamos sair da nossa própria vizinhança conceitual. É no cruzamento com a biologia de sistemas de organelas, com a bioeletricidade do desenvolvimento e com a física da matéria mole que residem as próximas grandes viradas da nossa bancada.

grandes_pesquisadores.instituicao: Department of Molecular Genetics, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot, Israel
grandes_pesquisadores.conceito_chave: Contactoma Celular & Comunicação Não-Vesicular de Organelas
grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Maya Schuldiner revolucionou a biologia celular ao quebrar o paradigma de que as organelas intracelulares se comunicavam exclusivamente através de vesículas secretoras (via clássica de Golgi e retículo).

Usando triagem robótica em larga escala de leveduras (SGA - Synthetic Genetic Array) combinada com microscopia de fluorescência de altíssima resolução, seu laboratório no Weizmann descobriu que organelas como retículo endoplasmático, mitocôndrias, peroxissomos, gotas lipídicas e vacúolos estão fisicamente conectadas por pontes proteicas especializadas ("tethers"), formando uma malha contínua chamada de 'contactoma'. Essas fendas de 10 a 30 nanômetros permitem o transporte ultrarrápido de lipídios, íons cálcio e intermediários metabólicos vitais, operando como cabos de alta velocidade dentro da célula.

grandes_pesquisadores.instituicao: Allen Discovery Center, Tufts University & Wyss Institute at Harvard University, USA
grandes_pesquisadores.conceito_chave: Bioeletricidade Morfogenética & Software Biológico de Tecidos
grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Michael Levin é pioneiro na redefinição da biologia do desenvolvimento e regeneração: enquanto a maioria dos biólogos encara eletricidade celular como algo restrito a neurônios e músculos, Levin provou que **todas as células vivas mantêm gradientes bioelétricos de membrana (Vmem)** e se comunicam através de junções comunicantes (gap junctions).

Seu grupo demonstrou que redes bioelétricas funcionam como um 'software de alto nível' que define a morfologia anatômica, a regeneração de membros e o comportamento inflamatório, conseguindo induzir o crescimento de olhos funcionais em caudas de girinos ou reprogramar tecidos apenas alterando a condutância iônica local.

temas_expansao.o_que_e: Como os gradientes elétricos trans-epiteliais e potenciais de membrana mantêm a ancoragem das junções oclusivas antes de danos estruturais.
temas_expansao.pergunta_provocativa: A permeabilidade da barreira hematoencefálica e da membrana peritrófica é controlada por campos bioelétricos antes de alterações estruturais?
temas_expansao.contexto:
O rompimento de junções oclusivas (claudina-5, occludina) tem sido estudado sob a ótica proteica e transcricional. No entanto, pesquisas bioelétricas comprovam que o potencial elétrico trans-epitelial mantém as moléculas de adesão sob tensão mecânica contínua.

Quando ocorre estresse oxidativo ou agressão por citocinas, a despolarização iônica precoce relaxa a força de ancoragem das claudinas, permitindo a passagem de fluidos e patógenos antes de qualquer degradação proteolítica visível.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Espectroscopia AFM-IR em Nanoescala (Photo-Thermal Induced Resonance)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Combinação de Microscopia de Força Atômica com Espectroscopia de Infravermelho (AFM-IR), permitindo caracterização química de espécies moleculares com resolução espacial de 10 a 20 nanômetros.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Durante décadas, a espectroscopia de infravermelho clássica (FTIR) foi limitada pelo limite de difração da luz óptica (~2 a 10 micrômetros), sendo incapaz de identificar compostos químicos dentro de organelas isoladas.

O desenvolvimento do AFM-IR contornou esse limite físico ao utilizar a ponta ultrafina de um microscópio de força atômica para detectar a expansão térmica nanomecânica da amostra quando excitada por um laser infravermelho pulsado e sintonizável. Com isso, tornou-se possível obter o espectro de absorção química exato de nanodomínios lipídicos, agregados amiloides e depósitos minerais sem marcadores fluorescentes.

tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Controle óptico remoto de neurônios, enterócitos e células musculares em mosquitos livres e intactos, usando luz vermelha profunda (CsChrimson) que penetra a cutícula sem lesão térmica.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Por décadas, testar a função de um circuito neuropeptídico ou da motilidade intestinal de um mosquito exigia dissecção traumática, microinjeção de drogas ou silenciamento por RNAi sistêmico (que afeta o inseto por dias).

A criação de canais de rodopsina de canal ativados por luz vermelha (CsChrimson, desenvolvidos por Boyden, Levin e colaboradores) permitiu que pesquisadores ativem subpopulações neurais e células enteroendócrinas específicas com um simples flash de LED vermelho enquanto o inseto voa ou se alimenta em tempo real, sem qualquer agulha ou anestesia.
